title: Simplexwise test for universal categorical equivalences
statement: Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices and degreewise pullbacks from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and categorical equivalences in the homotopy-category testing convention of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{p}S$ be maps of small simplicial sets in a fixed universe. For a small simplicial set $T$ with a map $t:T\to S$, put $X_T=X\times_S T$, $Y_T=Y\times_S T$, and $f_T=f\times_S\operatorname{id}_T$. Then the following conditions are equivalent: (i) $f_T$ is a categorical equivalence for every such $T,t$; (ii) for every $r\geq0$ and every simplex $\sigma:\Delta^r\to S$, the map $f_{\Delta^r}:X\times_S\Delta^r\to Y\times_S\Delta^r$ is a categorical equivalence. No quasicategory, fibration, injectivity or finiteness assumption is imposed on $X,Y,S,f,p,T,t$. Empty simplicial sets are allowed.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.2.8, printed p. 181 (PDF page 199): simplexwise criterion for categorical equivalences after every base change. Read online 2026-10-17; archival HTT copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: Condition (i) implies condition (ii) by specializing the arbitrary map $t:T\to S$ to $t=\sigma:\Delta^r\to S$.

Assume (ii) and fix $t:T\to S$. Every simplicial set $T$ is the filtered degreewise colimit of its finite sub-simplicial sets (finite means finitely many nondegenerate simplices), and the same finite subobjects form a filtered diagram in the slice over $S$ by restricting $t$. Degreewise pullback along $X\to S$ or $Y\to S$ commutes with this filtered colimit, since it is computed as reindexing of sets over each $S_n$. Therefore $X_T\to Y_T$ is the filtered colimit of the maps $X_{T_\alpha}\to Y_{T_\alpha}$; the filtered-colimit closure of categorical equivalences in [lem-coef-joyal-filtered-equivalences] reduces the proof to finite $T$.

Prove, by induction on the pair (dimension of $T$, number of nondegenerate simplices of $T$) ordered lexicographically, the claim: for every finite simplicial set $T$ and every map $t:T\to S$, the map $f_T$ is a categorical equivalence. The empty simplicial set is immediate, since both pullbacks are empty and the identity of $\varnothing$ is a categorical equivalence. Otherwise let $r=\dim T$, choose a nondegenerate $r$-simplex $\tau$ of $T$ and let $T'\subseteq T$ be the simplicial subset generated by the other nondegenerate simplices. Since no nondegenerate simplex of $T$ has dimension $>r$, the simplex $\tau$ is not a face of another nondegenerate simplex, so $T'$ contains every nondegenerate simplex except $\tau$. Applying [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] to $T'\hookrightarrow T$, the only cell outside $T'$ is $\tau$, so the filtration is constant except at stage $r$ and gives a pushout $T=T'\amalg_{\partial\Delta^r}\Delta^r$ along $\partial\Delta^r\hookrightarrow\Delta^r$, with $\Delta^r\to T$ the map classifying $\tau$ (it need not be injective, nor need the attaching map $\partial\Delta^r\to T'$). Here $T'$ has dimension $\leq r$ and fewer nondegenerate simplices, and $\partial\Delta^r$ (with the map $\partial\Delta^r\to\Delta^r\xrightarrow{\tau}T\to S$) has dimension $r-1$, so both precede $T$; for $r=0$, $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$. Degreewise pullback along $X\to S$ and along $Y\to S$ preserves pushouts, since in each degree $n$ it is the functor $X_n\times_{S_n}(-)$ on sets over $S_n$, which preserves pushouts; so $X_T=X_{T'}\amalg_{X_{\partial\Delta^r}}X_{\Delta^r}$ and likewise for $Y$, compatibly with $f$. The induction hypothesis applies to $T'$ and $\partial\Delta^r$, while (ii) applies to $\Delta^r\xrightarrow{t\tau}S$.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.2.8, proof, induction setup and pullback pushout formulas (printed pp. 181-182)

proof.text: The map of spans $(X_{T'}\leftarrow X_{\partial\Delta^r}\to X_{\Delta^r})\to(Y_{T'}\leftarrow Y_{\partial\Delta^r}\to Y_{\Delta^r})$ induced by $f$ has categorical equivalences as its three components, by the induction hypothesis and (ii). The legs $X_{\partial\Delta^r}\to X_{\Delta^r}$ and $Y_{\partial\Delta^r}\to Y_{\Delta^r}$ are degreewise injective, being degreewise pullbacks of the monomorphism $\partial\Delta^r\hookrightarrow\Delta^r$; the other legs need not be injective and no such hypothesis is used. By [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], simplicial sets with the Joyal model structure form a model category (complete and cocomplete, the limits and colimits being degreewise) whose cofibrations are the degreewise injective maps and whose weak equivalences are the categorical equivalences; since every map $\varnothing\to Z$ is injective, all six objects are cofibrant and the two injective legs are cofibrations. Part (b) of [lem-coef-model-cofibrant-colimit-comparison] then shows that the induced map of pushouts $X_T\to Y_T$, which is $f_T$ by step 3, is a categorical equivalence. (This is the assertion that HTT phrases as: by left properness these pushouts are homotopy pushouts.)

source.place: Proposition 3.2.2.8, proof, final homotopy-pushout comparison (printed p. 182)

proof.text: The induction proves the comparison for every finite sub-simplicial set of $T$, and the filtered-colimit step proves it for the original $T$. Since $T\to S$ was arbitrary, condition (i) follows, completing the equivalence.

split_report.summary: Expanded the HTT Proposition 3.2.2.8 proof into the filtered-colimit reduction, finite-cell induction, and the pushout comparison. No new DAG nodes were needed: the non-elementary inputs are the existing filtered-colimit closure of Joyal categorical equivalences, the Joyal model structure, the cube lemma for cofibrant spans, and the cell filtration of a monomorphism.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the auxiliary simplexwise-to-universal base-change calculation supporting the opening compactification/base-change argument of thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale; this calculation is not written as a separate paragraph in the blueprint proof.

tool_uses.why: Its filtered-colimit closure of categorical equivalences is the reduction from arbitrary T to finite sub-simplicial sets.
Its Joyal model structure supplies the cofibrations (monomorphisms) and weak equivalences (categorical equivalences) used in the finite pushout argument.
Its part (b), the cube lemma for spans of cofibrant objects with one cofibration leg, gives the comparison of the two pullback pushouts.
Mathlib leaf: the cell filtration of a monomorphism gives the one-cell pushout presentation of a finite simplicial set.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q01-be2a74140 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read HTT Prop. 3.2.2.8 and its proof (printed p.181) from a local copy another review had left in /tmp, since there is no network here; the archival-copy WANTED note stands. The item's statement matches the source exactly with Z=S and is not weakened. It adds no fibrancy, injectivity or finiteness hypothesis and allows empty sets. I tested T empty, S=Delta^0, r=0, degenerate sigma and non-injective characteristic maps; all are covered. Step 1 (specialisation) is correct. Step 2 is correct: the finite simplicial subsets of T form a filtered union, pullback is degreewise reindexing, and lem-coef-joyal-filtered-equivalences states exactly the closure used. Step 3 was marked elementary, had loose wording ('closure as Delta^r') and gave no citation or explicit inductive claim for the one-cell pushout. Repaired: it now cites the Mathlib leaf lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells, states the lexicographic induction, and notes the non-injective maps. Step 4 took a cube comparison that the cited left-proper statement does not give: replacing the B vertex would need a pushout along a non-cofibration (C3/C4, E5). It also named the wrong injective leg. Repaired: it now cites lem-coef-model-cofibrant-colimit-comparison (b), the cube lemma, using that all objects are cofibrant in the Joyal structure and that the legs X_{dDelta^r}->X_{Delta^r} are pullbacks of a monomorphism. The left-proper citation is dropped, and proof_deps and split_report.tool_uses are updated. The four cited nodes create no cycle. There are no new nodes. I found no duplicate: the three other 3.2.2.8-based nodes state different marked or base-invariance results. The accepted tool_uses are the joyal-filtered-equivalences, joyal-model-structure and model-cofibrant-colimit-comparison nodes. The corrected file is fixes/dag/nodes/sec-smooth-purity/lem-cbc-simplexwise-categorical-base-change.json.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
